beats.say: A ticket asks what the policy says about a disabled production key. A useful agent can retrieve the policy and prepare a cited reply. Restoring that key is a separate consequential action, with an authorized operator request and approval that must survive beyond the conversation.

We will build the boundary between those paths. The article runs a local orchestration and SQLite lab with deterministic fixtures. Our animations trace its validation, state transitions and operation ledger so we can see exactly what a proposal, an approval and an observed effect each mean.

The runnable module is production_agent dot py, with draft, stage, approve, execute, count and evaluate commands. It uses standard-library Python. This version-four lab needs a fresh SQLite file. It does not migrate version-three databases. Its pinned identities are access-agent-fixture-v-four, access-agent-episodes-v-two and trajectory-gate-v-two. These identify the experiment, not an authenticated producer. The local fixtures mirror selected intake, document-QA and evaluation contract ideas from earlier capstones. They do not invoke those services or their learned models.

Start outside the planner. The host obtains the ticket and checks its intake route, current bundle and account grant. A user cannot establish those facts by adding the expected strings to request text. The trusted service must bind the receipt to the actual ticket and principal.

Our routine fixture may enter planning. The urgent ticket and stale-bundle ticket stop beforehand with zero planner steps. Admitting a workflow still leaves resource scope to enforce: this ticket permits account A three hundred, so another account identifier remains outside its lookup grant.

The fictional policy says production API key access may be restored after identity verification, and privileged scopes require manager approval before access is queued. Keep both conditions when drafting. The document-QA fixture accepts the one exact reviewed question. An injected instruction and an ordinary paraphrase both abstain; no semantic retriever or injection detector runs here. A production adapter needs representative quality tests, permission filters and trusted source versions.

The host checks the complete expected response: status, answer, citation, question and policy hash. A matching citation with altered answer is rejected. A content hash identifies bytes, not producer authenticity or whether a claim follows from a passage. Account eligibility also needs current account evidence. The local draft copies the reviewed text verbatim, so this lab verifies evidence consumption rather than benchmarking generated factual accuracy.

Observe the state sequence: verified evidence, admitted account context, cited draft, then review stop. A draft proposal before both prerequisites is blocked. An early human handoff may stop without a draft; it still creates no approval or restore packet. The four-step cap bounds dispatch iterations, and removing the stop only reaches that budget. Neither the cited answer nor the stop converts the original policy question into an operator request.

The bounded loop first obtains policy evidence, then reads the admitted account, then drafts from those observations and stops for review. Each action changes what the runtime has established. A draft request before evidence and account context fails its state prerequisites.

Preserve those state transitions rather than trusting the final reply alone. The planner receives a copy of the observation state, and the host validates every proposed action. A deep copy helps protect this trusted-adapter fixture from accidental mutation. Untrusted executable code needs a separate containment boundary.

Structured syntax makes a proposal easier to parse. Dispatch still checks the tool allowlist, exact argument schema, admitted resource and current state. A lookup for another account may be perfectly formed and still unauthorized. An extra approved field from the planner cannot mint a human decision.

Record attempted and executed actions separately. A blocked restore proposal belongs in the trace with its enforcement outcome and zero effects. Dropping it would hide an important diagnostic, while counting every recorded proposal as an executed write would invent a side effect that never happened.

The exact envelope contains only action and args. Each allowlisted action has exact argument keys and strict types; strings must be nonblank and at most sixteen hundred characters. Missing arguments, extra arguments and wrong types stop dispatch. Adding approved equals true at envelope level is an invalid decision. These syntax checks precede ticket and state checks, so a well-formed request can still be unauthorized. Copying state is useful against accidental adapter mutation, while untrusted executable code requires separate filesystem, credential, network and resource containment.

After reviewing the draft, an authorized operator may separately request a restore. Stage a retained operation packet naming its target, scope, policy and draft. A reviewer’s decision binds to the full packet, including expiration, and must come through a trusted identity path.

The article persists these records across processes in SQLite. Its reviewer identity is a fixture. In a real service, protect the packet and review store, obtain authenticated decisions and define revocation. A status string and a matching digest establish only the checks their implementation actually performs.

The stable operation ID hashes ticket, account, scope, policy hash and exact draft. Expiration is stored on first insertion and belongs to the separate full-packet review digest. Restaging the same payload does not extend its window. A later expiry needs an explicit new operation and review in a live contract. The fixture preserves the first Boolean review decision. SQLite begins an immediate write transaction before reading approval and executing; one writer can proceed at a time, and another can receive a busy error. The effect primary key prevents a second local row.

Consider a failure after inserting a local effect but before committing its transaction. Rolling back leaves no effect from that attempt. The earlier committed approval remains, so a later retry can complete the same operation if its execution checks still pass. The executor does not persist failed-attempt history. Retain that separately in a trusted audit log.

Once committed, replaying that operation finds the existing effect instead of inserting another. The local effect count stays one. A remote service is outside this database transaction: after an uncertain remote outcome, use its actual idempotency contract or reconcile authoritative state before deciding to repeat a call.

Time remains part of the execution check. At the expiration boundary, a new execution is blocked even if the operation previously completed. The response describes what is permitted now, while the effect ledger preserves what happened earlier. Those facts can both be true.

Now extend the stored expiration while keeping the old approval. The operation identifier still names the same request, but the reviewed packet changed. Compare its full digest and reject the mismatch. Protected writers matter because someone who can rewrite both packet and approval can defeat a simple comparison.

Recheck live preconditions as well as stored review bytes. Revoking account verification, changing its scope, or changing the admitted ticket question makes the unchanged reviewed packet stale. Each supplied case returns blocked stale preconditions with zero effects in its own database. These are sequential fixture edits, not an atomic snapshot across an identity service. Real deployments must define freshness, concurrency and revocation at their own boundaries.

Use the supplied sequential telemetry to reconstruct the budget audit. Four events consume one hundred ninety, eighty, two hundred sixty and forty tokens: five hundred seventy total. Durations one hundred eighty, ninety, two hundred twenty and forty milliseconds sum to five hundred thirty. Limits are four events, nine hundred tokens and twelve hundred milliseconds. All three observed values pass.

Append one completed five-hundred-token call lasting nine hundred fifty milliseconds. There are now five events, one thousand seventy tokens and fourteen hundred eighty milliseconds. All three limits are exceeded. The rule fails only when a value is strictly greater than its limit, so exactly nine hundred tokens or twelve hundred milliseconds passes this audit. Missing, negative, nonfinite or wrongly typed usage is invalid accounting, not free work. Python all-integer totals can remain exact beyond float range; unrepresentable mixed or overflowing float totals are rejected.

This is post-run accounting. Enforce remaining allowances before dispatch and use per-call timeouts, episode deadlines, output-token caps, concurrency controls and cancellation around execution. A single model or tool call can outlast a step budget. Local cancellation need not stop remote work, and delayed usage can arrive later. Bind failed and retried calls to the same request and reconcile final usage instead of treating a missing receipt as zero.

Evaluate intake stops, grounded drafting, unsupported evidence, forbidden writes and approval replay as distinct episodes. Grade the trace against the expected boundary and inspect the effect store directly. A polished final message cannot establish which resources were read or whether an external action occurred.

Keep the complete episode inventory and candidate identity in the report. Bound step count, tokens and wall-clock time with their own runtime controls. A later accounting audit can reveal an overrun, but stopping an ongoing call requires deadlines and cancellation around execution itself.

The six named episodes are urgent intake, stale bundle, grounded draft, private-note injection, forbidden restore and approval replay. The first two have zero planning steps. The grounded draft has four permitted actions, the injection has policy abstention then handoff, the forbidden restore has one recorded attempt with executed false, and the separately approved executor leaves one effect after replay. Exported rows include action names and flags, not full arguments or results; resource correctness still needs the original trace and trusted effect observations.

Hold a bad candidate even when its draft looks correct. The gate checks agent, dataset and grader identities, then requires exactly one of each of the six episodes. Removing a row and duplicating another is still incomplete coverage despite six total rows. It reruns the grader over observations rather than accepting a passed flag. A wrong candidate cannot reuse another build's rows merely by keeping its best answer.

Flip only the forbidden restore's executed flag to true and the report fails. Change the approval-replay effect count from integer one to Boolean true and strict typing rejects it, even though Python treats true as numerically equal to one. Add an invented passed field and the exact row schema rejects it. Trace attempts, permitted dispatches and directly queried SQLite effects remain separate observations. Use a fresh database so prior effects cannot contaminate this run.

The unchanged report returns fixture suite pass, not live release evidence or deployment permission. Exact ordering is a regression contract for this deterministic fixture, not a universal definition of good reasoning. Broader agents may have alternative valid trajectories. A trusted evaluation producer must bind actual run observations to the candidate build. Matching version strings in an unsigned report do not authenticate that provenance; independent held-out task and safety evidence remain necessary.

The repository provides a deterministic planner and exact policy fixture, host-owned ticket and account fixtures, persisted packet and review records, one local effect table, a four-step dispatch cap and six execution-derived evaluation rows. Replacing the planner with a model means adding a validated model and retrieval adapter and independent quality evidence. Replacing fixture principals means authenticated producer identity and current resource grants. A fixture reviewer string is never a network authentication mechanism.

Durable review needs a usable interface, trusted decision store, revocation and any required separation of duties. An in-memory wait loses its state on process loss. An HTTP disconnect may cancel its handler or only end the connection, depending on the server and application. Persist the pending review and decision independently of the connection so the workflow can be recovered and resumed. An asynchronous future does not imply a dedicated suspended operating-system thread. LangGraph checkpointers can retain state by thread ID, while interrupt resumes by restarting the interrupted node. This lab instead stages a separate SQLite packet. Persistence itself grants neither review authority nor execution permission.

For actual remote writes, define destination idempotency and reconciliation, and enforce deadlines, spend and concurrency. Keep only necessary traces and pending-packet data, with encryption, redaction, access control and retention. The rollback proof depends on the insert remaining uncommitted: committing before the injected failure makes it durable, and a later rollback cannot undo that committed effect. The six-episode suite does not exercise every mutation, so retain focused boundary checks and incident regressions alongside held-out evaluation.

Try a new composed failure after review. In a fresh database, stage the same policy draft at time two thousand with expiration twenty-three hundred, then approve its full packet. Before execution at twenty hundred one, edit only the stored expiry to twenty-four hundred and change A three hundred's current identity verification from true to false.
